blocks.text: HOARDING CLEANOUT FAQ
Frequently Asked Questions About Hoarding Cleanouts in Etobicoke

items.q: How much does a hoarding cleanout cost in Etobicoke?
a: Pricing is based on how many rooms are affected and how much sorting the belongings need — never on whether the property is a house or a condo. The figure is confirmed free at a private walkthrough.

items.q: Can you handle a hoarding cleanout in our condo along the lakeshore?
a: Yes, and it’s handled by the building’s book. Certificates of insurance go to management at booking, freight elevators reserve ahead, and timing is arranged so hallways and common areas see nothing unusual.

items.q: Our bungalow is original to the fifties or sixties — does that change the approach?
a: Yes, in a good way. The crew understands what a smaller, original-footprint home from that era typically involves, and plans for it rather than treating it the same as a much newer, larger property.

items.q: What's the best way to clean out a hoarder's house?
a: Professional help, a clear plan, and patience. Going in without a strategy usually causes more distress than progress. The most effective approach sorts systematically — keep, donate, recycle, dispose — and moves at a pace the household can genuinely handle.

items.q: Can you handle a larger property near the Kingsway with real discretion?
a: Yes — grounds, driveways and privacy get the same consideration as the rooms inside, with discreet scheduling available on request.

items.q: What happens if we find valuables, documents or sentimental items?
a: They’re set aside immediately and brought to the family, never sorted into a donation or disposal pile by default.

items.q: What if the property has safety hazards — pests, mould, structural damage?
a: Those get flagged honestly. Live Junk Free doesn’t disturb suspected biohazards or structural issues — the concern is identified and the household is pointed toward the right licensed specialist before the rest of the cleanout proceeds.

items.q: Can the cleanout happen while the person continues living in the home?
a: Yes, and it’s one of the most common ways a hoarding cleanout actually happens. Work can proceed room by room while the resident stays in place throughout.
